findings.section: Design S2 step 5 (also research.md D5; contracts/speckit-package-cli.md S2 step 4; quickstart.md SF)
findings.note: Specified screen invocation 'detect-secrets scan --force-use-all-plugins <abs dest dir>' empirically scans zero files and exits 0 on pinned detect-secrets 1.5.0/Windows (non-git destination; git ls-files enumeration). Blocking compliance gate is vacuous as specified. Fix: cwd=destination + 'scan --all-files' (verified working) + assert scan coverage >= inventory count.
No positive-control test that a planted secret fails assembly; quickstart F only asserts empty results, so a no-op scan passes all planned checks.

Claim that the screen covers 'exactly the delivered bytes including freshly generated docs' is overstated: SNAPSHOT.json and the marker are written after the screen and never scanned; they embed unscreened free-text label/captured-by/source-ref.
Destination existing as a regular file/symlink is not an enumerated exit-2 refusal; behavior falls to incidental mkdir errors.

Packager imports underscore-private helpers from speckit_bootstrap, whose bytes are simultaneously a frozen captured asset; no stability contract pins this coupling - add an import-surface test or installer-side note in tasks.
'OK 151 files verified' hard-codes the count the plan says is never hard-coded; goes stale on any manifest edit.
Regex alone permits empty segments (a//b) and omits reserved-name/trailing-dot rules; schema-only validators get weaker guarantees than the prose implies (procedural validation acknowledged).
Label uniqueness is asserted but unenforced/unregistered; should be stated as a human convention in the package README.
